Subject: MAP checkpoint — pricing/budget alignment for Finexa deal

Hi Olivia / Carlos —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our MAP (attached), wanted to run the weekly checkpoint focused on pricing and finance approvals so we can lock the close timeline. High-level status:

- Evaluation: Prod pilot running (2 seats) — ingestion and latency tests trending positive.
- Commercial: initial pricing reviewed; Finexa requested an additional discount and a credit for POC tokens.
- Legal/Procure: procurement looped in for PO / T&Cs next week.

Today's goals:
1) Confirm pricing path (one-time credit vs. % discount on commit)
2) Agree commit sizing and term to meet internal discount thresholds
3) Identify who needs to sign off on internal finance/discount approvals and expected timing

Action items / owners (please confirm or edit):
- Finexa to confirm preferred structure: 6-month commit vs. 12-month (owner: Olivia) — due 2026-03-05
- Redwood to propose final term sheet & credit schedule (owner: Marissa) — due 2026-03-04
- Finance approval for requested discount level (owner: Aditya) — internal target 2026-03-05
- Legal to prepare PO/DocuSign (owner: Karthik) — target 2026-03-08

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v3.pdf (MAP with milestones), Pricing_Term_Sheet_Finexa_v2.xlsx (proposed rate card + credit options).

Questions for today:
- Carlos — can you confirm whether procurement prefers a committed monthly minimum or a prepaid credit drawdown?
- Olivia — if we offered a consumption credit (one-time) vs. an 18% committed discount, which structure helps budget reporting for you?

I'll be on the 11:00am PT check; if you prefer a different cadence for approvals we can adapt.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks, received. Quick answers:
- Procurement prefers a committed monthly minimum tied to a term (easier for our FP&A).
- That said, we can accept a blended approach (smaller committed minimum + drawdown credits for POC over first 60 days).

Primary constraint: our Q2 budget needs the cost to be recorded as a committed subscription not a one-off professional credit; can you confirm if the one-time credit can be applied as an invoiced negative line item on the subscription (so it reduces committed spend)?

I can be on the 11:00am PT sync. I'll loop procurement@finexa.com for PO questions.

Folks —

Quick internal update ahead of the 11am: Finance is willing to approve up to an 18% effective discount on a 12-month commit and up to 12% on a 6-month commit. We should avoid ad-hoc one-time credits that reduce the visibility of committed ARR; instead recommend structuring as:

- Option A (preferred by Redwood / cleaner ARR): 12-month commit with 18% discount, billed monthly; include a starting credit pool (contract line item) that draws down for POC usage during month 1–2.
- Option B: 6-month commit with 12% discount + larger POC credit applied as a pre-paid drawdown.

If Finexa must show the discount as a reduction on subscription line items, legal can represent the credit as a negative subscription line (Aditya -> Karthik to confirm exact billing coding). Karthik — can you flag whether Legal needs Finance to prepare any exceptional accounting language?

Owner notes:
- I will own the finance approval flow and will push to have final sign-off by EOD 2026-03-05 if we get confirmed commit sizing today.
- Sergio, please have SE confirm expected token usage for the 6-month vs 12-month scenarios so we can finalize cost math. Dev, can you drop estimated monthly tokens by end of day?

Aditya
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
